P01.title: Patch Ivanti Connect Secure on vpn-gw-01 to close internet path to the domain controller
P01.summary: Validated path P01 starts at the corporate remote access VPN (vpn-gw-01, Ivanti Connect Secure), which is exposed to the internet and affected by CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887. The validation agent gained an authenticated shell on vpn-gw-01. Admin credentials cached on vpn-gw-01 also work on the IT admin jump host (jump-it-01). The jump host admin group has RDP rights on the domain controller (dc-01), which the agent reached with read-only rights. Fixing vpn-gw-01 breaks the path at its entry point.
P01.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take over the corporate VPN, reuse admin credentials stored on it to log on to the IT jump host, and from there open a session on the domain controller. Control of the domain controller would let an attacker control accounts and access across the corporate network, opening the door to ransomware and wide disruption of utility business operations. Both flaws are heavily exploited in the wild, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the Ivanti Connect Secure web and admin interfaces on vpn-gw-01 to only the networks that need them, and remove admin interface exposure to the internet.

Upgrade vpn-gw-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-46805, CVE-2024-21887); if no fix or mitigation is available, follow the KEV required action to discontinue use of the product.
Check vpn-gw-01 for signs of compromise, such as unknown files, accounts or configuration changes, and rebuild the appliance from a clean image if any are found.
Reset all admin credentials cached on vpn-gw-01, and work with the Windows Server team to reset the same credentials wherever they are reused on jump-it-01 so they no longer match.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-01 reports the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs and that its admin interface is not reachable from the internet.
Confirm the old admin credentials from vpn-gw-01 no longer authenticate on vpn-gw-01 or jump-it-01.
Request a rerun of the validation of path P01 to confirm it no longer reaches dc-01.
P01.exec_line: An internet-facing VPN flaw lets attackers reach our main domain controller; patching the VPN and resetting its admin passwords closes this path.
P01.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P02.title: Fix Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 to close the field office VPN path to the domain controller (P02)
P02.summary: Validation confirmed path P02: an out-of-bounds write flaw (CVE-2024-21762) in the Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 gave an internet foothold. The Print Spooler flaw (CVE-2021-34527) on file server fs-02 then gave SYSTEM rights. A cached domain admin logon stored on fs-02 exposed credentials that reach domain controller dc-01. Fixing the entry point on vpn-gw-02 breaks the whole path.
P02.why_it_matters: An outside attacker with no password could go from the field office VPN to full control of Active Directory on dc-01. That would let them sign in anywhere on the corporate network, disable defenses, and stage ransomware against business and operations systems. Both flaws are known to be used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict the Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 (Remote access VPN, field offices) to known field office source addresses, or disable the SSL-VPN portal until it is patched.
Upgrade FortiOS on vpn-gw-02 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-21762). If no fix can be applied, discontinue use of the SSL-VPN as the KEV required action states.
After upgrading, check vpn-gw-02 for signs of compromise: unexpected admin accounts, configuration changes, and unusual VPN sessions or logins since February 2024.
End all active SSL-VPN sessions and reset credentials for local admin and VPN accounts on vpn-gw-02. Tell the Windows Server and Identity teams if any compromise is found.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-02 reports the vendor's fixed FortiOS release and that the SSL-VPN is reachable only from the approved source addresses.
Review the vpn-gw-02 admin account list and configuration against a known-good baseline and confirm no unexpected entries.
Request a rerun of the validation for attack path P02 to confirm the entry step on vpn-gw-02 no longer succeeds.
P02.exec_line: An internet-facing field office VPN flaw could let attackers take over our main corporate directory; Network Engineering is patching and locking it down.
P02.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P03.title: Patch the contractor gateway (nsg-01) to stop session takeover that leads to the email server
P03.summary: Validated path P03 starts at the Citrix NetScaler Gateway contractor gateway (nsg-01), which is internet facing. CVE-2023-4966 on nsg-01 leaked session tokens, which allowed a contractor session to be taken over. From that session the Microsoft Exchange Server email server (exch-01) responded to a server-side request forgery check for CVE-2022-41040. Fixing nsg-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P03.why_it_matters: An outsider could take over a contractor's remote access session and reach the corporate email server from inside the network. From there they could read or abuse company email, which could support fraud, data theft, or a ransomware attack that disrupts business operations. Both weaknesses are widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 to known contractor source addresses, or take it off the internet until it is patched.
Upgrade the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-4966).
Right after the upgrade, kill all active and persistent sessions on nsg-01, as the KEV required action demands, so no stolen session token stays valid.
Check nsg-01 for compromise by reviewing session and authentication logs for sessions reused from unexpected addresses or devices, and report any findings to the security team.
Reset passwords for contractor accounts that had sessions on nsg-01 during the exposure period.
verify_steps: Confirm in the nsg-01 management console that the Citrix NetScaler Gateway reports the vendor's fixed release.
Confirm that no sessions created before the upgrade remain active on nsg-01.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P03 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P03.exec_line: An internet-facing contractor access gateway lets outsiders hijack sessions and reach company email; Network Engineering will patch it and reset sessions.
P03.route_reason: The path ends at exch-01, the email server, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes straight to Network Engineering, owner of nsg-01.

P04.title: Patch GlobalProtect on plant edge firewall fw-edge-03 to cut the internet path to the plant data historian
P04.summary: Path P04 starts at fw-edge-03, the plant edge firewall running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS with GlobalProtect, where CVE-2024-3400 was confirmed exploitable from the internet. The firewall's management account password is the same as the local admin password on ot-jump-01, the IT to OT jump host, and hist-01, the plant data historian, accepts logons from that jump host. The validation agent stopped at the OT boundary and did not log on to the jump host or the historian. Fixing the firewall breaks the path at its entry point.
P04.why_it_matters: An unauthenticated attacker on the internet could take full control of the plant edge firewall, reuse its management password to log on to the IT to OT jump host, and from there reach the plant data historian. That would put an outsider inside the OT boundary with access to operational plant data and a foothold toward control systems. This flaw is widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, on fw-edge-03 (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS), enable the Threat Prevention IDs available from the vendor for this flaw and confirm they apply to traffic reaching the GlobalProtect portal, and limit firewall management access to internal admin networks only.
Upgrade fw-edge-03 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-3400).
After upgrading, check fw-edge-03 for signs of compromise, including unexpected files, accounts, configuration changes or outbound connections, and escalate to incident response if any are found.

Change the fw-edge-03 management account password to a new unique value, and work with OT Engineering to change the matching local admin password on ot-jump-01 so the two never share a credential again.
verify_steps: Confirm fw-edge-03 is running the vendor's fixed release and that the Threat Prevention IDs are active on the GlobalProtect portal traffic.
Confirm with OT Engineering that the fw-edge-03 management password no longer matches the ot-jump-01 local admin password.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P04 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P04.exec_line: A widely exploited flaw in a plant edge firewall could let outsiders reach our plant data historian; we are patching it and changing shared passwords.
P04.route_reason: The path ends at hist-01, the plant data historian, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P05.title: Patch internet-facing Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 (Vendor file exchange) to close SQL injection
P05.summary: Validation path P05 confirmed that the internet-facing Progress MOVEit Transfer web application on mft-01 (Vendor file exchange) is vulnerable to CVE-2023-34362, an unauthenticated SQL injection. The tester confirmed the flaw by reading only the version table, with no further data access. mft-01 is both the entry point and the target of this path, so fixing it closes the path.
P05.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could reach the MOVEit Transfer database on mft-01 without logging in, then read, change or delete the files and records the utility exchanges with its vendors. That could expose sensitive business and operational data, disrupt vendor exchanges, and trigger notification and regulatory obligations. This flaw has been widely exploited, including in ransomware data theft campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict HTTP and HTTPS access to the Progress MOVEit Transfer web interface on mft-01 so that only approved vendor and internal source addresses can reach it, until patching is complete.
Apply updates per vendor instructions: upgrade Progress MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-34362).

After patching, check mft-01 for signs of compromise, including unexpected files in the web application folders, unknown or recently created user accounts, and unusual file downloads in the MOVEit Transfer logs; escalate to the security team if anything is found.
Reset the MOVEit Transfer administrator and service account credentials on mft-01 and end all active user sessions.
verify_steps: Confirm in the MOVEit Transfer admin console on mft-01 that the installed version matches the vendor's fixed release.
Confirm from an outside network address that is not on the approved list that the mft-01 web interface cannot be reached.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P05 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P05.exec_line: Our internet-facing vendor file exchange has a widely exploited flaw that could expose shared files; patching it is underway.
P05.route_reason: The path ends at mft-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to the Enterprise Applications team.

P06.title: Close internet-reachable admin setup flaw on Partner wiki (wiki-ext, Atlassian Confluence Data Center)
P06.summary: Validation confirmed that the Partner wiki (wiki-ext), an internet-facing Atlassian Confluence Data Center instance, exposes a setup endpoint affected by CVE-2023-22515 that would let an outsider create a Confluence administrator account. The agent reached the endpoint from the internet and stopped before creating an account. Fixing wiki-ext closes the whole path.
P06.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could make themselves an administrator of the Partner wiki and read, change or delete everything shared there with partners, including any project documents, contacts or credentials stored on pages. They could also use that admin access to plant malicious content for partners or as a foothold for further attacks, and this flaw is widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, restrict internet access to the Partner wiki (wiki-ext) so that only known partner and staff addresses can reach it, and block external access to its setup endpoints until it is patched.
Upgrade Atlassian Confluence Data Center on wiki-ext to the vendor's fixed release for CVE-2023-22515, applying the vendor's mitigations if the upgrade cannot happen immediately.

As CISA requires, check wiki-ext for evidence of compromise: review the Confluence administrators group and user list for unexpected or recently created admin accounts, and look for unexplained plugins or configuration changes.
Remove any unauthorized accounts found, reset passwords for legitimate Confluence administrators, and report any positive findings to the security team so they can be reported to CISA.
verify_steps: Confirm in the Confluence administration console that wiki-ext is running the vendor's fixed release for CVE-2023-22515.
From outside the network, confirm the setup endpoints on wiki-ext are no longer reachable and that the administrators group contains only approved accounts.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P06 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P06.exec_line: Our internet-facing partner wiki has a widely exploited flaw letting outsiders make themselves administrators; we are restricting access and patching it now.
P06.route_reason: The path ends at wiki-ext, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it can go straight to the Collaboration Tools team.

P07.title: Close unauthenticated setup wizard on ScreenConnect remote support console (rmm-01) to cut path to virtualization cluster
P07.summary: Validation confirmed that the internet-facing ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote support console (rmm-01) exposed its setup wizard without authentication (CVE-2024-1709), allowing creation of an administrator account. From there, an attacker could create the directory group that the VMware ESXi virtualization cluster (esxi-07) trusts for admin access (CVE-2024-37085) and take full control of the hosts. Fixing rmm-01, the entry point, breaks the whole path.
P07.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could take over the remote support console and then gain full control of the virtualization cluster that runs corporate servers. That would let them shut down, encrypt or steal many systems at once, disrupting business operations across the utility. Both weaknesses are used in active ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, remove internet access to the ConnectWise ScreenConnect management interface on rmm-01, allowing only approved internal or VPN addresses until patched.

Upgrade ConnectWise ScreenConnect on rmm-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs, applying mitigations per vendor instructions, or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
After upgrading, check rmm-01 for compromise: review all ScreenConnect user accounts, remove any unknown administrator accounts, and review session and login history for unexpected activity.
Reset passwords for all ScreenConnect administrator accounts and any directory credentials stored on or used by rmm-01, and end all active sessions.
Ask the Infrastructure team to confirm the directory group trusted by esxi-07 for admin access was not created or changed by accounts linked to rmm-01.
verify_steps: Confirm from an external network that the ScreenConnect management interface on rmm-01 is no longer reachable from the internet and the setup wizard cannot be reached without authentication.
Confirm the ScreenConnect version on rmm-01 matches the vendor's fixed release and that only approved administrator accounts exist.
Request a rerun of the validation of path P07 to confirm the path from rmm-01 to esxi-07 is closed.
P07.exec_line: Our internet-facing remote support tool could let attackers take over the server virtualization cluster; we are restricting access and patching it now.
P07.route_reason: The path ends at esxi-07, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it can go directly to the IT Service Desk owner of rmm-01.

P08.title: Close internet-exposed Cisco IOS XE web UI on substation router rtr-sub-12 (path P08 to EMS data link)
P08.summary: Validated path P08 starts at rtr-sub-12, the Substation comms router running Cisco IOS XE, whose web UI is reachable from the internet and runs a version affected by CVE-2023-20198. From that router a route reaches ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, with no access list between the substation comms network and the EMS data link. No traffic was sent to the EMS link during validation. Fixing the router's internet exposure and vulnerability breaks the path at its entry point.
P08.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take full control of the substation router without a password and then reach the energy management system data link, which has no filtering in between. That link carries data used to monitor and run the grid, so access to it could disrupt operator visibility or control of substations. This flaw is among the most widely exploited in the world.
fix_steps: Today, take the Cisco IOS XE web UI on rtr-sub-12 off the internet by disabling the HTTP and HTTPS server, or limiting it to trusted management networks only, as required by BOD 23-02.
Upgrade Cisco IOS XE on rtr-sub-12 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-20198).
Check rtr-sub-12 for signs of compromise, such as unknown local accounts with privilege level 15 or unexpected configuration changes, and immediately report any positive findings to CISA.
Remove any unauthorized accounts and reset all local and management credentials on rtr-sub-12.
verify_steps: From an outside network, confirm the web UI on rtr-sub-12 no longer responds on HTTP or HTTPS.
Confirm rtr-sub-12 is running the patched Cisco IOS XE release and that its local account list contains only approved accounts.
Ask the security validation team to rerun validation of path P08 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P08.exec_line: An internet-exposed substation router could let outsiders reach our grid energy management link; the router is being locked down and patched now.
P08.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P09.title: Patch Log4j2 in the internet-facing Outage map API (outage-api) to close remote code execution path P09
P09.summary: The autonomous validation tool confirmed that the Outage map API (outage-api), an internet-facing Java service using Apache Log4j2 owned by Customer Applications, is exploitable through CVE-2021-44228. A harmless test value sent in a request header caused outage-api to make an outbound DNS query. This shows the vulnerable Log4j2 lookup behavior is reachable from the internet. The path has one step, so fixing outage-api closes it completely.
P09.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could run their own code on the Outage map API server and use it as a foothold inside the utility's network. They could also tamper with or take down the public outage map that customers rely on during storms and emergencies. This flaw is among the most widely exploited ever and is known to be used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, cut exposure on outage-api. Either take the Outage map API off the internet, or block its outbound network connections to the internet, until the update is in place. This interim measure is acceptable only until the update is applied.

Update Apache Log4j2 in the outage-api Java service to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2021-44228), rebuild, and redeploy. If it cannot be updated, remove outage-api from the network, as KEV requires.
After patching, check outage-api for signs of compromise. Look for unexpected processes, files, scheduled tasks, or outbound connections since the service was first exposed.
Rotate any credentials, API keys, and service account secrets stored on or used by outage-api.
verify_steps: Confirm that every Log4j2 library in the deployed outage-api build and its dependencies is at the vendor's fixed release, with no older copies left anywhere in the deployment.
Confirm that outage-api makes no unexpected outbound DNS or other external connections when it handles normal requests.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P09 against outage-api and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P09.exec_line: Our public outage map service has a widely exploited flaw letting outsiders take control; the application team should patch it immediately.
P09.route_reason: The path ends at outage-api, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it can go straight to the owning team, Customer Applications.

P10.title: Close unauthenticated takeover of Fortinet FortiManager fmgr-01 from the corporate user network
P10.summary: The validation tool confirmed that the device registration port on fmgr-01 (Fortinet FortiManager, Firewall manager) answers from the corporate user network while running a version affected by CVE-2024-47575, a missing authentication flaw that lets a remote attacker run commands without logging in. This single step gives an attacker control of the firewall manager.
P10.why_it_matters: fmgr-01 holds the configuration for the firewalls it manages and can push changes to them. An attacker who controls it could weaken or rewrite firewall rules across the utility, read stored device credentials, and open paths toward more sensitive networks. This flaw is among the most widely exploited in the wild.
fix_steps: Today, restrict the device registration port on Fortinet FortiManager fmgr-01 so only the managed firewalls' addresses can reach it, and block it from the corporate user network.
On fmgr-01, turn off acceptance of unknown devices so only firewalls you have already approved can register.
Upgrade fmgr-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs, applying the vendor's mitigations if an upgrade cannot be done right away.
After upgrading, check fmgr-01 for compromise: look for unknown registered devices, unexpected admin accounts, and unexplained configuration changes pushed to managed firewalls.
Reset fmgr-01 admin passwords and the credentials it stores for managed firewalls, and treat them as exposed if any sign of compromise is found.
verify_steps: From a host on the corporate user network, confirm the fmgr-01 device registration port no longer answers.
Confirm fmgr-01 reports the vendor's fixed release and that unknown device registration is disabled.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P10 to confirm it no longer succeeds.
P10.exec_line: Our firewall management server can be taken over from the office network; we are restricting access and patching it now.
P10.route_reason: The path ends at fmgr-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to Network Engineering.

P11.title: Patch Netlogon (Zerologon) on domain controller dc-01
P11.summary: The validation tool confirmed that domain controller dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory) runs a version affected by CVE-2020-1472 (Zerologon) and accepts Netlogon secure channel connections from corporate workstations. The agent checked the version only and made no change. This is a one-step path: any device on the corporate network could reach the flaw directly.
P11.why_it_matters: An attacker on any corporate workstation could take over the domain controller and, with it, every user account, server and system that trusts Active Directory. That would let them deploy ransomware across the business network or move toward operational systems, and this flaw is widely exploited in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, limit which networks can reach Netlogon and RPC on dc-01 to the corporate segments that need it, and block it from any untrusted or guest segments.
Apply the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs to dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory), following Microsoft's update instructions.
Turn on Netlogon enforcement mode on dc-01 so it requires secure RPC for all machine accounts, and only allow exceptions for named devices that have been reviewed.
Check dc-01 for signs of compromise: unexpected resets of the domain controller machine account password, new or changed privileged accounts, and unusual replication or logon activity.
If any sign of compromise is found, reset the dc-01 machine account password and the krbtgt account password twice, and escalate to incident response.
verify_steps: Confirm the vendor's fixed release is installed on dc-01 and that Netlogon enforcement mode is active.
Review dc-01 system event logs to confirm vulnerable Netlogon connection attempts are being denied rather than allowed.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P11 against dc-01 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P11.exec_line: Our main corporate login server has a widely exploited flaw that could let an attacker control the whole business network; patching is underway.
P11.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, which is marked as a crown jewel asset.

P12.title: Restrict RDP and require multi-factor sign-in on OT jump host ot-jump-01 to close the corporate path to EMS data link ems-link-01
P12.summary: Validated path P12 runs from the corporate network to the energy management system data link (ems-link-01) through the IT to OT jump host (ot-jump-01). The validation tool reached the RDP sign-in prompt on ot-jump-01, a Microsoft Windows Server in the OT DMZ, from a corporate desktop VLAN. That prompt accepts a password only, with no multi-factor step. The tool did not attempt a logon. ems-link-01 trusts logons that come from ot-jump-01, so anyone who signs in to the jump host with a stolen or guessed password could move on to the EMS data link. Fixing access to ot-jump-01 breaks the whole path.
P12.why_it_matters: An attacker with one stolen corporate password could sign in to the OT jump host from any desktop and then reach the energy management system data link, which trusts the jump host. That could expose or tamper with the data grid operators rely on to monitor and control the power system. Both assets on this path are crown jewels for the utility.
fix_steps: On the IT to OT jump host ot-jump-01 (Microsoft Windows Server), change the firewall rules today so RDP is accepted only from a named set of approved administrator workstations or a dedicated admin network, not the whole corporate network.
Require multi-factor authentication for every RDP sign-in to ot-jump-01, and remove password-only sign-in for all accounts that can reach it.
Limit the accounts allowed to sign in to ot-jump-01 to the named OT engineers and operators who need it, and remove shared or unused accounts.

Review ot-jump-01 sign-in logs for logons from corporate desktop networks that are not on the approved list. If any are unexplained, treat the host as possibly compromised, end those sessions, and reset the affected account passwords.
verify_steps: From an ordinary corporate desktop VLAN, confirm the RDP sign-in prompt on ot-jump-01 can no longer be reached.
From an approved administrator workstation, confirm that signing in to ot-jump-01 requires a multi-factor prompt and fails with a password alone.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P12 and confirm it no longer reaches ems-link-01.
P12.exec_line: Any corporate computer could reach the gateway into our grid control systems with only a password; we are locking it down and requiring multi-factor sign-in.
P12.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel, and the fix point ot-jump-01 is also a crown jewel.
